ca-tre-kho-gung.name: Vietnamese catfish braised with ginger
aliases: Catfish braised with ginger and coconut water
ca-tre-kho-gung.serving_basis: Four servings of catfish braised with young ginger and fresh coconut water.
ca-tre-kho-gung.description: Catfish is marinated with fish sauce, caramel and pepper, then braised with young ginger in fresh coconut water. Bep Viet adapts the documented method for a family meal, finishing the sauce with a little rice flour for a light gloss.
ca-tre-kho-gung.finished_dish: Tender, firm catfish pieces in a glossy amber coconut sauce with young ginger, shallots and chili.
ca-tre-kho-gung.serving: Serve from the clay pot or transfer to a shallow dish. Spoon the sauce over the fish and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Choose young ginger for a fragrant flavor without bitterness.
Marinate the fish for about 20 minutes before braising.
Mix rice flour with a little water and add it after the fish is cooked; stop when the sauce is lightly thickened.
search_terms: Braised fish dish served with rice
ca-tre-kho-gung.image_alt: Catfish braised with young ginger in glossy caramel coconut sauce in a clay pot.
ca-tre-kho-gung.time_note: About 1 hour and 15 minutes, including 20 minutes of marinating.

ingredients.name: Cleaned catfish
ingredients.notes: Cut into pieces about 2 cm thick and drain.

ingredients.name: Young ginger
ingredients.notes: Rinse, keep the skin on and slice.

ingredients.name: Bird's-eye chilies
ingredients.notes: Crush or leave whole according to heat preference.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fresh coconut water
ingredients.notes: Use as the braising liquid.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Mix with a little cold water to thicken the sauce.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the fish and sauce.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For cleaning and light seasoning.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the shallots.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the marinade and finish the dish.

ingredients.name: Caramel sauce
ingredients.notes: Adds color to the braise.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the savory seasoning.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Mix with rice flour before adding to the pot.

preparation_steps: Clean the catfish, rub with salt to remove slime and odor, rinse and cut into thick pieces.
Rinse the young ginger and slice it. Mince the shallots and crush the chilies.
Marinate the fish with fish sauce, salt, sugar, pepper and caramel sauce for about 20 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat oil in a clay pot and fry the shallots until fragrant. Add the fish and turn gently until the surface firms; pour in the marinade.
Add coconut water, bring to a boil and skim. Lower the heat, add ginger and chili, then braise gently until the fish is cooked and the sauce has reduced. Turn the fish carefully.
Mix rice flour with water, pour it into the pot gradually and simmer until the sauce lightly thickens. Taste, finish with pepper and turn off the heat.

keywords: Catfish braised with ginger and coconut water

banh-duc-nong-ha-noi.name: Hanoi hot rice cake with pork and mushrooms
aliases: Hanoi hot rice cake with minced pork
banh-duc-nong-ha-noi.serving_basis: Six bowls of soft hot rice cake topped with pork, mushrooms and dipping sauce.
banh-duc-nong-ha-noi.description: Hanoi bánh đúc nóng is a soft, thick rice cake served warm with minced pork, wood ear, shiitake, fried shallots and a tangy-salty-sweet fish-sauce dressing. Bếp Việt adapts the published home recipe and stirs the batter over low heat until smooth and translucent.
banh-duc-nong-ha-noi.finished_dish: A warm ivory rice cake with a soft, chewy texture, savory pork-and-mushroom topping, crisp fried shallots and fresh cilantro.
banh-duc-nong-ha-noi.serving: Spoon the hot rice cake into bowls, add the pork and mushroom topping, fried shallots and cilantro, then pour over a little dipping sauce. Serve immediately.
tips: Stir the batter before heating and keep stirring as it cooks to prevent lumps and scorching.
Soak and rinse the wood ear and shiitake well, then chop them finely.
Add the dipping sauce a little at a time so the rice cake does not become too salty.
search_terms: Hanoi hot rice cake with minced pork
Hanoi rice cake with pork and wood ear
Hanoi banh duc with wood ear mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms
banh-duc-nong-ha-noi.image_alt: Hanoi hot bánh đúc topped with minced pork, wood ear, shiitake, fried shallots and cilantro.
banh-duc-nong-ha-noi.time_note: About 1 hour and 55 minutes, including a one-hour batter soak.

preparation_steps: Mix the rice flour, glutinous rice flour and salt. Stir in clear limewater and stock or water until smooth, then soak for about one hour.
Soak the wood ear and shiitake until soft, rinse and chop. Season the pork with a little fish sauce and pepper.
Mince the shallots, rinse and chop the cilantro. Mix fish sauce, vinegar, sugar and water for the dipping sauce; taste and adjust.
cooking_steps: Cook the batter over low heat, stirring continuously until it turns smooth, glossy and thick with no raw-flour smell.
Fry the shallots until fragrant. Add the pork and stir to break it up; add wood ear and shiitake and cook until done.
Spoon the hot rice cake into bowls, top with the pork mixture, fried shallots and cilantro, then add dipping sauce to taste. Serve immediately.

banh-mi-que-hai-phong.name: Hai Phong pâté bread sticks
banh-mi-que-hai-phong.serving_basis: Eight small pâté-filled bread sticks served with mildly spicy chí chương.
banh-mi-que-hai-phong.description: Hai Phong breadsticks are simple with a thin, crispy loaf, a layer of fragrant fatty liver pate and spicy chili. Viet Kitchen edited a home version using pre-prepared pate from a reliable source, heating the cake close to eating to keep the crust crispy.
banh-mi-que-hai-phong.finished_dish: Golden crisp bread sticks with a soft crumb and fragrant pâté, dipped in gently spicy red chí chương.
banh-mi-que-hai-phong.serving: Split the warm bread lengthwise, spread with pâté and toast once more. Serve chí chương separately so everyone can adjust the heat.
banh-mi-que-hai-phong.image_alt: Golden, crisp Hai Phong bread sticks, one split and filled with pâté, served with a small bowl of red chí chương chili sauce.
banh-mi-que-hai-phong.time_note: Use pre-prepared pate to shorten the time; Baking time depends on the oven and loaf thickness.
tips: Choose cooked, packaged pâté and follow its storage instructions; do not leave it at room temperature for long.
Toast the bread just before serving; adding pâté too early will soften the crust.
Chí chương is distinctly hot; add a little at a time, or use red chili sauce if it is unavailable.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese bread sticks
ingredients.notes: Choose freshly baked sticks with a moderately soft crumb and thin crust.

ingredients.name: Prepared liver pâté
ingredients.notes: Use a cooked product and keep it refrigerated as directed on the label.

ingredients.name: Chí chương chili sauce
ingredients.notes: Hai Phong chili sauce; red chili sauce may be substituted.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: Optional; soften before spreading with the pâté.

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.notes: Optional for this home-style version; cut into thin batons.

preparation_steps: Preheat an oven or air fryer to 180°C. Keep the pâté refrigerated until ready to spread and portion the chí chương into a small bowl.
Make a lengthwise slit in each roll without cutting it all the way through. If using cucumber, wash and cut it into thin batons.
cooking_steps: Toast the bread for 3–4 minutes until hot and crisp but not hard; adjust for its size and your appliance.
Spread a thin layer of pâté inside each roll, add a little butter if desired and toast for another 1–2 minutes until the filling is hot.
Serve the bread while crisp, with chí chương and cucumber on the side. Do not leave pâté-filled bread out for long.

com-hen-hue.name: Hue clam rice
aliases: Cold rice mixed with Hue mussels
com-hen-hue.serving_basis: Four bowls of clam rice with herbs, peanuts, pork cracklings and fermented shrimp paste, served with hot clam broth.
com-hen-hue.description: Hue mussel rice combines cold rice, small mussels, sliced ​​vegetables, peanuts, pork rinds and shrimp paste; Hot mussel broth is often served with it. Vietnamese kitchens calibrate ingredients for the family tray, keeping each layer of ingredients separate for diners to mix according to taste.
com-hen-hue.finished_dish: Fluffy rice topped with fragrant clams, crisp fresh greens, nutty peanuts and crunchy pork cracklings, with clear hot clam broth on the side.
com-hen-hue.serving: Arrange the rice, herbs, clams, peanuts and pork cracklings in bowls. Serve with hot clam broth and diluted fermented shrimp paste; mix just before eating.
com-hen-hue.image_alt: A bowl of Hue clam rice with stir-fried clams, finely cut herbs, peanuts, pork cracklings and a small cup of hot clam broth.
com-hen-hue.time_note: The time it takes to clean mussels depends on the amount of sand and type of mussels; Always filter the boiled water before using.
tips: Use clean clams, cook them completely and strain out all grit; bring the broth to a boil before keeping it hot for serving.
If cooking rice ahead, cool it quickly, refrigerate it and use it the same day; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature for long.
Fermented shrimp paste is salty and intense; dissolve it and add gradually so it does not overpower the clams.
keywords: Cold rice mixed with Hue mussels

ingredients.name: Fresh clams in their shells

ingredients.name: Pork cracklings

ingredients.name: Fresh chili

ingredients.name: Cooking oil

preparation_steps: Soak the clams in clean water, changing it and rinsing repeatedly to remove grit. Wash the herbs, thinly slice the banana blossom and starfruit, and soak the blossom in diluted lime water.
Rinse and cook fluffy rice. If preparing ahead, spread it in a thin layer to cool quickly, then refrigerate; prepare the roasted peanuts and pork cracklings.
Mince the shallots and garlic; chop the Vietnamese coriander and chili. Mix the fermented shrimp paste with a little warm water, let it settle and strain until smooth.
cooking_steps: Put the clams in a pot of water and cook until the shells open. Remove the meat and strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve to remove grit. Bring the clear broth back to a boil, then keep hot.
Sauté the shallots and garlic, add the clams and quickly toss with fish sauce and a little diluted fermented shrimp paste. Turn off the heat once warmed so the clams do not become tough.

Divide the rice among bowls and arrange the clams, banana blossom, pennywort, Vietnamese coriander, starfruit, peanuts and pork cracklings in separate portions. Serve with hot clam broth and shrimp paste to mix to taste.

keywords: Cold rice mixed with Hue mussels

che-bap-con-hen-hue.name: Con Hen Island sweet corn pudding, Hue
che-bap-con-hen-hue.serving_basis: Four bowls of gently sweet young-corn pudding, with coconut milk to taste.
che-bap-con-hen-hue.description: Con Hen corn sweet soup takes advantage of the sweet and fragrant taste of young corn, cooked with boiled water and sugar to create a soft sweet soup. Viet Kitchen edited the family version to be less sweet, with a thin layer of coconut milk to keep the corn flavor at the center.
che-bap-con-hen-hue.finished_dish: A golden bowl of sweet corn pudding with plump tender kernels, lightly thickened syrup and a little fragrant coconut cream.
che-bap-con-hen-hue.serving: Spoon into bowls and serve warm, or cool and chill. Add the coconut milk just before serving so the corn remains the main flavor.
che-bap-con-hen-hue.image_alt: A golden bowl of Con Hen Island sweet corn pudding, with tender young corn in lightly thickened syrup and coconut cream.
che-bap-con-hen-hue.time_note: Softness depends on the maturity of the corn; Older corn takes longer to cook and may be less sweet.
tips: Choose young, milky corn and cut close to the cob while keeping the kernels whole and avoiding the tough core.
Stir gently after adding the tapioca starch so the kernels stay intact.
If using fresh coconut milk, heat it gently with a pinch of salt and use it the same day.
keywords: Con Hen Island sweet corn pudding, Hue

ingredients.name: Young waxy corn
ingredients.notes: Choose young, plump ears and shave the kernels thinly from the cob.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For simmering the cobs to flavor the liquid.

ingredients.name: Rock sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust for the corn's natural sweetness.

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch
ingredients.notes: Dissolve in 40 ml cold water to thicken the pudding lightly.

ingredients.name: Coconut milk
ingredients.notes: For drizzling on top; optional.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: A small pinch to balance the sweetness.

ingredients.name: Pandan leaves
ingredients.notes: Wash and tie into a bundle for a delicate aroma.

preparation_steps: Remove the husks and silk and rinse the corn. Carefully shave off the kernels with a sharp knife, keeping the cobs to flavor the cooking liquid.
Dissolve the tapioca starch in cold water. Tie the pandan leaves into a bundle and set out the rock sugar and coconut milk.
cooking_steps: Add the corn cobs and pandan leaves to a pot of water and simmer gently for about 12 minutes. Remove them and strain the liquid if it contains corn fragments.
Add the corn kernels to the cooking liquid and simmer over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until tender but intact. Add the rock sugar and salt and stir to dissolve.
Slowly pour the dissolved tapioca starch into the pot, stirring gently until it reaches the desired consistency. Cook for 1–2 minutes more, then turn off the heat.
Warm the coconut milk separately over low heat until hot and lightly thickened. Spoon the pudding into bowls, drizzle with a little coconut milk and serve warm or chilled.

keywords: Con Hen Island sweet corn pudding, Hue
